title: Secure boot: never run a fake program
what: The boot check of a small processor: it compares the program's signature (an 8-bit tag here) with the expected one and answers ACCEPT or REJECT.
why: If a glitch makes the check say ACCEPT for a wrong signature, the chip runs the attacker's program.
teaches: How many glitches a real protection (three compares, each owning its own state bits, plus an alarm) forces the attacker to use.
lesson_after: One compare falls to one glitch. Three compares plus an alarm need three well-timed glitches: the protection raises the cost, it does not make the attack impossible. More glitches at the right moments are much harder to do in a laboratory.
